questions.text: In order that Benjamin might be brought to Egypt, Joseph detained
questions.explanation: Joseph detained Simeon and bound him before their brothers' eyes as a guarantee that they would return with Benjamin.

questions.text: According to Jeremiah's prophecy, the domination of nations by Nebuchadnezzar was
options: the result of his military might.
the result of the wickedness of nations.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah taught that Nebuchadnezzar was God's servant and his domination was part of God's divine purpose.

questions.text: Ezekiel was ordered to eat... and then go to speak to the house of Israel.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to eat the scroll containing God's words before going to speak to Israel.

questions.text: The place where Abraham was asked to sacrifice Isaac was
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:2 states that God told Abraham to go to the land of Moriah to offer Isaac as a sacrifice.

questions.text: The one who was to be the wife of Isaac was known
options: by her coming to the well to draw water.
because she was a descendant of Abraham's brother.
because she said 'Drink, and I will water your camels'.
questions.explanation: Rebekah was identified as the chosen wife because she offered to water Abraham's servant's camels.

questions.text: Achan was
options: one of the spies who visited Rahab in Jericho.
one of the two men who prophesied in the camp in the wilderness.
one of the judges of Israel.
the one who took some of the devoted things when Jericho fell.
questions.explanation: Achan took devoted items from Jericho, which caused Israel's defeat at Ai.

questions.text: 'How is it you were not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the Lord's anointed?' was said by
options: Elijah to Ahab when Ahab sought to kill him.
David to the Amalekite who claimed to have killed Saul.
Joab to Absalom when the latter rebelled against David.
David to Saul when Saul attacked him with a spear.
questions.explanation: David said this to the Amalekite who claimed to have killed Saul, then had him executed.

questions.text: The prophet regularly addressed as 'son of man' was
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is repeatedly addressed as 'son of man' throughout his book.

questions.text: What was the last miracle God performed before the Israelites were released from Egypt?
options: Thick darkness brought about by the hot wind 'Khamisin'.
The slaughter of the first born.
questions.explanation: The final plague was the death of the firstborn, which finally convinced Pharaoh to release Israel.

questions.text: Who was the prophet who proved on Mount Carmel that Yahweh is greater than Baal?
questions.explanation: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, and God sent fire from heaven.

questions.text: On the third day of creation God made
questions.explanation: On the third day, God created dry land, seas, and vegetation.

questions.text: The Lord said to Moses: 'Cut two tablets of stone like the first; and I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets which you broke.' On what occasion was this said?
options: At the renewal of the Covenant.
Just before the election of Joshua.
After the first fall of Manna from heaven.
questions.explanation: After Moses broke the first tablets, God commanded him to cut new tablets to renew the covenant.

questions.text: The city of Jericho was captured by the Israelites
options: after a fierce battle lasting seven days.
because the army of the city was betrayed by some of its soldiers.
because the defence system was very weak.
at the blast of the trumpets of the priests.
questions.explanation: Jericho fell when the priests blew trumpets and the people shouted, causing the walls to collapse.

questions.text: The call of Isaiah took place
options: on the return from the Babylonian captivity.
in the year of the death of King Uzziah.
during the dedication of the temple by king Solomon.
shortly before the rise of the Maccabees.
questions.explanation: Isaiah received his call in the year King Uzziah died (Isaiah 6:1).

questions.text: When Zechariah doubted the announcement of the birth of John he
questions.explanation: Zechariah was struck dumb because he did not believe Gabriel's message.

questions.text: Herod wanted to kill the child Jesus because
options: he thought he would become a prophet.
he learnt that he was born king of the Jews.
he was born of a virgin.
questions.explanation: Herod felt threatened when he learned that a king of the Jews had been born.

questions.text: What is the main lesson of the parable of the prodigal son?
options: A son should always obey his father.
God forgives those who sincerely repent.
questions.explanation: The parable teaches that God joyfully forgives sinners who repent and return to Him.

questions.text: 'These men who have turned the world upside down have come here also, and Jason has received them.' Which town is referred to here?
questions.explanation: This accusation was made in Thessalonica when Paul and Silas preached there.

questions.text: 'And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High', refers to
questions.explanation: Zechariah prophesied that his son John the Baptist would be called a prophet of the Most High.

questions.text: The parable of the mustard seed teaches that
options: the kingdom of God is invisible.
although the kingdom of God is for all, very few enter it.
the kingdom of God will expand world-wide from what appears to be an insignificant beginning.
It is not certain when the kingdom of God will come.
questions.explanation: The mustard seed, though tiny, grows into a large tree, representing the growth of God's kingdom.

questions.text: When the women got to the tomb of Jesus they found the stone rolled away and
options: saw Jesus coming out of the tomb.
Jesus was no longer in the tomb.
Jesus was sitting in the tomb.
immediately saw a vision of Jesus.
questions.explanation: The women found the tomb empty; Jesus had already risen from the dead.

questions.text: 'You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and ... and to the end of the earth.
questions.explanation: Jesus told His disciples they would be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.

questions.text: Paul was first arrested in Jerusalem because he
questions.explanation: Paul was arrested because Jews from Asia accused him of bringing Greeks into the temple.

questions.text: Which country in Africa provided Jesus with a refuge when Herod sought to destroy him?
questions.explanation: Joseph took Jesus and Mary to Egypt to escape Herod's order to kill all male infants.

questions.text: 'After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie'. Who said this?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this about Jesus, acknowledging His supremacy.

questions.text: Who addressed Jesus at Jericho, saying, 'Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me?
questions.explanation: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, cried out to Jesus for mercy.

questions.text: By whom did the Lord heal the blindness of Paul?
questions.explanation: Ananias was sent by God to heal Paul's blindness and baptize him.

questions.text: Who insisted in his speech that God does not dwell in houses made with hands and that it was wrong for Solomon to have built a house for Him?
questions.explanation: Stephen said this in his speech before the Sanhedrin, quoting Isaiah.

questions.text: 'The Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God'. This was said by the angel Gabriel to
questions.explanation: Gabriel said these words to Mary during the annunciation.

questions.text: 'But I say to you that hear, love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who abuse you'. Jesus said this
options: During the Sermon on the Mount.
questions.explanation: This is part of Jesus' teaching in the Sermon on the Mount.

questions.text: What did the Apostles do when complaints were made to them that some sections of the new Christian community were not being supplied with their needs for sustenance? They
options: gave out more money for buying food.
said that they had neither gold nor silver.
appointed seven deacons to undertake the care of the new Christians.
appointed the Apostles: James, Peter and John to oversee the supply of provisions to the new Christians.
questions.explanation: The apostles appointed seven deacons to handle the distribution of food to widows.

questions.text: When Paul came to Rome, the first set of people to whom he preached were the
questions.explanation: Paul first addressed the Jewish leaders in Rome.

questions.text: 'Blessed are you among women and blessed is the fruit of your womb'. This was said by
questions.explanation: Elizabeth said this to Mary when she visited her.

questions.text: Jesus was led into the wilderness by
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

questions.text: And he came to ... where he had been brought up; and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath Day, and stood up to read. Identify the missing place in the above text.
questions.explanation: Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up, and read in the synagogue.

questions.text: 'Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven for they all had her?' This question was put to Jesus by the
questions.explanation: The Sadducees, who did not believe in the resurrection, asked Jesus this question.

questions.text: Pilate gave Jesus to the Jews to be crucified because
options: he found Jesus guilty of the charges.
the Jews brought pressure upon him.
questions.explanation: Pilate gave in to the pressure from the Jewish crowd, though he found no fault in Jesus.

questions.text: Paul was converted so that he might
options: not be killed for his sins.
bear the name of the Lord before the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: Paul was chosen to bear Christ's name before Gentiles, kings, and the people of Israel.

questions.text: Paul and Silas were imprisoned at
questions.explanation: Paul and Silas were beaten and imprisoned in Philippi after casting out a spirit from a slave girl.

questions.text: After the Flood, God allowed all food to be eaten except
options: flesh with its blood in it.
questions.explanation: God forbade eating flesh with its blood, as life is in the blood.

questions.text: 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples, born of you shall be divided ...'. This was addressed by God to
questions.explanation: God told Rebekah that she carried two nations in her womb, Jacob and Esau.

questions.text: The wife of Moses was
questions.explanation: Moses' wife was Zipporah, daughter of Jethro.

questions.text: 'I the Lord your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, but showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments'. This statement was made by God when
options: He gave the Ten Commandments to Moses.
the family of Aaron was elected to the priesthood.
He commanded Moses to go to meet Pharaoh.
questions.explanation: This was part of the second commandment given to Moses at Mount Sinai.

questions.text: The three sons of Noah were Shem, Ham and
questions.explanation: Noah's three sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

questions.text: For rebelling against Moses and God, the Israelites were bitten by the fiery snakes. The cure for the snakebites was
options: a drink of the water from the rock
anointing the affected part of the body with oil
to call on the name of Yahweh
a look at the bronze serpent
questions.explanation: God instructed Moses to make a bronze serpent; whoever looked at it would live.

questions.text: Joshua was appointed to lead the Israelites to the Promised Land because
options: Moses was too old to lead them there
the Israelites preferred Joshua to Moses
Moses never returned from Mount Sinai
of Moses' rebellion in the wilderness of Zin
questions.explanation: Because Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it, he was not allowed to enter the Promised Land.

questions.text: The covenant was renewed on Mount Sinai because
options: there was a new generation which did not remember the first
the people had taken part in Korah's rebellion
the people had demanded water from the rock
Aaron had made a golden calf
questions.explanation: The covenant was renewed after the people sinned with the golden calf.

questions.text: Those inspired by God to lead the tribes of Israel in battle were the
questions.explanation: God raised up judges to deliver Israel from their enemies.

questions.text: Each of the spies sent out by Moses on God's command to report on the nature of the Promised Land was a
questions.explanation: Each spy was a leader from his respective tribe.

questions.text: God revealed to Samuel that he was going to punish Eli because he
options: did not correct his sons' sinful behaviour
did not offer sacrifice as the law required
did not warn the people of Israel to stop sinning
warned his sons but did not punish them
questions.explanation: Eli failed to restrain his sons from their sinful behavior.

questions.text: The sun stood still when
options: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt
Jericho fell to the army of Joshua
Noah came out of the ark
Joshua defeated the Amorites at Gideon
questions.explanation: Joshua prayed for the sun to stand still during his battle against the Amorites.

questions.text: 'I repent that I made Saul king'. What incident does this refer to?
options: During Saul's encounter with the Ammonites.
When Saul disobeyed God over Amalek.
questions.explanation: God regretted making Saul king after he disobeyed regarding the Amalekites.

questions.text: David's first reaction after he had been rebuked by God through the prophet Nathan for his sin against Uriah and with Uriah's wife was to
options: plead with God to preserve the life of his child by Uriah's wife
request that the punishments threatened by God would not come to pass
ask Nathan to beg Uriah's wife to pardon him
questions.explanation: David pleaded with God to spare the life of the child born to Bathsheba.

questions.text: 'If he (Baal) is a god, let him contend for himself because his altar has been pulled down'. Who pulled down the altar?
questions.explanation: Gideon pulled down the altar of Baal at night.

questions.text: Hannah prayed to God at Shiloh for a son because
options: Elkanah hated her for being barren
She had sinned against the Lord
questions.explanation: Hannah was distressed because Peninnah, her rival, provoked her over her barrenness.

questions.text: God pronounced utter destruction on the Amalekites because
options: they were hostile to the Kenites who lived among them
they were hostile neighbours of Israel like the Philistines
Saul desired to acquire the Amalekite territory
they opposed Israel on their way from Egypt to the promised land
questions.explanation: The Amalekites attacked Israel when they came out of Egypt.

questions.text: As David was about to die, he charged Solomon to keep God's statutes, commandments, ordinances and testimonies, so that he, Solomon, might
options: prosper and the Davidic dynasty be preserved forever
have children who would succeed him
questions.explanation: David instructed Solomon to obey God so that he would prosper and David's line would continue.

questions.text: In the trade treaty between king Solomon and Hiram of Lebanon, Solomon was to supply wheat and oil while Hiram was to supply
questions.explanation: Hiram supplied Solomon with timber from Lebanon.

questions.text: To whom was this addressed? 'Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke upon us and we will serve you'.
questions.explanation: The people made this request to Rehoboam, Solomon's son.

questions.text: 'I have been very jealous for the Lord, the God of hosts' for the people of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I even I only, am left; and they seek my life to take it away.' This was said by
options: Elijah at a cave in Mount Carmel
Moses at a cave in Mount Horeb
Elijah at a cave in Mount Horeb
questions.explanation: Elijah said this to God at Mount Horeb, complaining that he alone remained faithful.

questions.text: 'Thus saith the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, Amend your ways and your doings. Trust not in lying words saying: 'The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord'. This message was given by
questions.explanation: Jeremiah delivered this message in the temple, warning of judgment.

questions.text: Which prophet gave this cry? 'Woe is me! For I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips'.
questions.explanation: Isaiah cried this when he saw the Lord in the temple.

questions.text: The prophet who proclaimed a new covenant of God with Israel and Judah was
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied about the new covenant God would make with Israel and Judah.

questions.text: The synoptic gospels refer to the
options: first four books of the New Testament
first three books of the New Testament
first five books of the Bible
questions.explanation: The synoptic gospels are Matthew, Mark, and Luke.

questions.text: 'And he will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children'. The person whose future work was being described here was
questions.explanation: John the Baptist was described as going before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah.

questions.text: He said therefore to the multitudes ... 'You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?' Who was the speaker?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this to the multitudes coming for baptism.

questions.text: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God' was said by Jesus to
options: the leper who asked to be cleansed
questions.explanation: Jesus said this in response to Satan's temptation to jump from the temple.

questions.text: The people of Nazareth found it difficult to believe what Jesus preached to them because they
questions.explanation: The people of Nazareth knew Jesus from childhood and did not accept His authority.

questions.text: In the parable of the sower, the seeds on the good ground are meant to represent those who
options: accept and live by God's word
questions.explanation: The good ground represents those who hear and live by God's word.

questions.text: Who is being referred to here? 'But he went out and began to talk freely about it, and to spread the news, so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a town, but was out in the country; and people came to him from every quarter.
questions.explanation: The leper cleansed by Jesus spread the news freely, preventing Jesus from entering towns openly.

questions.text: 'An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, but no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah,' According to St. Matthew, Jesus said this to the
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to the Pharisees and Sadducees who asked for a sign.

questions.text: And Jesus said to them, 'Follow me and I will make you fishers of men.' This was addressed to
questions.explanation: Jesus called Simon Peter and Andrew first, telling them they would become fishers of men.

questions.text: Hosanna means
questions.explanation: Hosanna means 'save now' or 'save, we pray'.

questions.text: One of the reasons why Jesus denounced the Scribes and Pharisees was that they
options: did not practice what they preached
did not preach regularly in the temple
took great care of the tombs of their ancestors
questions.explanation: Jesus denounced the Scribes and Pharisees for hypocrisy — they did not practice what they preached.

questions.text: Simon the Cananaean was
options: the Pharisee in whose house the woman anointed Jesus
the one who carried Jesus' cross
questions.explanation: Simon the Cananaean was one of the twelve apostles.

questions.text: The reason why Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Salome went to where Jesus was buried on the third day after the burial was to
options: plead with the soldiers who were keeping watch there
see if the body of Jesus was still there
weep at the tomb according to the custom of the Jews
questions.explanation: The women went to the tomb to anoint Jesus' body with spices.

questions.text: To some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised others, Jesus told the parable of the
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parable of the Pharisee and the tax-collector to those who trusted in their own righteousness.

questions.text: The main reason why Peter and John were arrested by the officers of the Temple after they had cured the lame man at the gate called beautiful was that they
options: abused the elders of the people
questions.explanation: Peter and John were arrested because they were proclaiming the resurrection of Jesus.

questions.text: The conversion of Paul was made possible by
questions.explanation: Paul was converted when he encountered the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus.

questions.text: Who is being referred to here? 'Let his habitation become desolate, and let there be no one to live in it' and 'His office let another take'.
questions.explanation: This refers to Judas Iscariot, whose office was taken by Matthias.

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT one of the decisions of the Jerusalem Council communicated to Gentile Christians?
options: Abstinence from eating meat offered to idols.
Avoidance of eating meat with blood in it.
Abstinence from eating strangled animals' flesh.
questions.explanation: The council did not require circumcision; they required abstinence from idols, blood, strangled meat, and fornication.

questions.text: The proconsul when Paul arrived in Corinth was called
questions.explanation: Gallio was proconsul of Corinth when Paul was brought before him.

questions.text: Identify the speaker: 'Now, I know that the Lord has sent his angel to deliver me out of the hand of Herod and from everything that the Jewish people expected to happen to me'.
questions.explanation: Peter said this after an angel delivered him from prison.

questions.text: The seven deacons were appointed to
options: conduct a mission to the Gentiles
help in the distribution of food
questions.explanation: The seven deacons were appointed to oversee the daily distribution of food.

questions.text: Which ruler said this in the course of Paul's defense? 'In a short time you think to make me a Christian!'
questions.explanation: King Agrippa said this to Paul during his defense.

questions.text: When Paul arrived in Rome, the people he first addressed were
options: the local leaders of the Jews
The Roman soldiers who were guarding him
The pagans whom he wanted to convert
questions.explanation: Paul first summoned the local Jewish leaders in Rome.

questions.text: 'For I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.' Who was this devoted person?
questions.explanation: Paul said this to the elders at Ephesus, showing his commitment to Christ.

questions.text: Complete the quotation which relates to Paul's voyage to Rome: 'Do not be afraid, Paul, you must stand before Caesar, and lo...'
options: Ceasar will give you a favorable judgment
All who seek your life will perish
I have a large number of disciples in Rome
God has granted you all those who sail with you
questions.explanation: An angel told Paul that God had granted him all those who sailed with him.

questions.text: According to Genesis Chapter 1, on the 6th day, God created
questions.explanation: On the sixth day, God created land animals and man in His image.

questions.text: The flood lasted while Noah was in the ark, for
questions.explanation: The flood waters prevailed upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.

questions.text: 'Walk before me, and be blameless.' How old was the addressee when this voice came?
questions.explanation: Abraham was 99 years old when God appeared to him and established the covenant.

questions.text: 'You would bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to Sheol.' Jacob said this to his children because
options: He feared that Benjamin would be lost to him like Joseph.
questions.explanation: Jacob feared losing Benjamin as he had lost Joseph.

questions.text: And the magician said to Pharaoh, 'This is the finger of God'. This statement was made after the plague of
questions.explanation: The magicians said this after the plague of gnats, which they could not replicate.

questions.text: The father of Moses was of the tribe of
questions.explanation: Moses' father, Amram, was from the tribe of Levi.

questions.text: When did the Israelites say 'All that the Lord has spoken we will do'?
options: When Moses spoke to them before his death
After the incident of the golden calf
questions.explanation: The Israelites made this declaration at Mount Sinai when God gave the law.

questions.text: The 5th of the Ten Commandments is a warning
options: not to bow down to idols
to honour one's father and mother.
questions.explanation: The fifth commandment is 'Honor your father and your mother'.

questions.text: 'Hear now, you rebels: shall we bring forth water for you out of this rock?' Was spoken by Moses
questions.explanation: Moses spoke these words in the wilderness of Zin at Meribah.

questions.text: The spies sent out into the land of Canaan were NOT required to find out whether the
options: people who dwelt in it were few or many
land they dwelt in was good or bad
cities they dwelt in were camps or strongholds
land was flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: The spies were not sent to find out if the land was flowing with milk and honey; they were to scout the land and its people.

questions.text: Who was chosen to lead the Israelites after Moses' death?
questions.explanation: Joshua was chosen by God to succeed Moses.

questions.text: Joshua's first victory was in
questions.explanation: Joshua's first victory was at Jericho.

questions.text: Sisera was put to death by
questions.explanation: Jael killed Sisera by driving a tent peg through his temple.

questions.text: 'But I will be with you and you will smite the Midianites as one man' was said by God to
questions.explanation: God said this to Gideon when calling him to deliver Israel from Midian.

questions.text: The name 'Samuel' means
options: I have asked him of the Lord
questions.explanation: Samuel means 'asked of God' because Hannah had prayed for him.

questions.text: Samuel's sons were rejected as judges because
options: they were not from the royal family
they perverted justice and took bribes
questions.explanation: Samuel's sons took bribes and perverted justice, leading the people to demand a king.

questions.text: God took the Kingdom from Saul because he
options: did not offer sacrifices to the Lord
disobeyed the Lord by offering burnt sacrifices himself
questions.explanation: Saul lost the kingdom because he disobeyed God's command and offered a burnt sacrifice himself.

questions.text: How was Saul killed?
options: He took his own sword and fell upon it.
questions.explanation: Saul fell on his own sword to avoid being captured by the Philistines.

questions.text: The commander of David's army was
questions.explanation: Joab was the commander of David's army.

questions.text: King David committed adultery with
questions.explanation: David committed adultery with Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite.

questions.text: Which prophet encouraged Jeroboam I to revolt at the initial stage?
questions.explanation: Ahijah the prophet told Jeroboam that he would rule ten tribes of Israel.

questions.text: The city of Samaria was built by
questions.explanation: Omri, king of Israel, purchased the hill of Samaria and built the city.

questions.text: The prophet from Tekoah was
questions.explanation: Amos was a shepherd from Tekoah who prophesied to Israel.

questions.text: Which king reigned after Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: Manasseh succeeded his father Hezekiah as king of Judah.

questions.text: Which was NOT a complaint of the people when Nehemiah was rebuilding Jerusalem?
options: Let us get grain; that we may eat and keep alive.
We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses.
The strength of the burden-bearers is failing.
We are forcing our sons and daughters to be slaves.
questions.explanation: The complaints included famine, mortgaging fields, and enslaving children — not failing burden-bearers.

questions.text: Jesus was said to be 'of Nazareth' because
options: his ancestor David lived in Nazareth
he was brought up in the city of Nazareth
he made Nazareth his preaching headquarters.
questions.explanation: Jesus was called a Nazarene because He was brought up in Nazareth.

questions.text: 'You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?' was part of the Preaching of
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this to the multitudes coming to be baptized.

questions.text: Which of these statements is correct?
options: The order in which Jesus was tempted varies in Matthew and Luke but the tests remain the same.
Matthew follows Luke's order in which Jesus was tempted.
The temptation story of Jesus is found in Mark only.
Only Luke gives us the story of Jesus temptation.
questions.explanation: The order of Jesus' temptations differs between Matthew and Luke, though the tests are the same.

questions.text: Who of these was NOT one of the twelve?
questions.explanation: Luke was a physician and companion of Paul, not one of the twelve apostles.

questions.text: Who said 'I am not worthy to have you come under my roof'?
questions.explanation: The centurion at Capernaum said this, expressing his humility and faith in Jesus.

questions.text: 'The Kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in field'. This parable teaches about the
options: urgency of entry into the Kingdom
questions.explanation: The parable teaches that the kingdom of heaven is of great value and hidden to many.

questions.text: The renowned interpreters of the Mosaic Law in the time of Jesus were the
questions.explanation: The Scribes were experts in interpreting the Mosaic Law.

questions.text: 'This is my beloved son: listen to him', was said
questions.explanation: God spoke these words at the Transfiguration of Jesus.

questions.text: 'The Kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seeds in his field; but while men were sleeping his enemy came and sowed weeds amongst the wheat, and went away.' The owner of the field was
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that the owner of the field is the Son of Man.

questions.text: When Herod the Tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus, he thought that He was
options: John the Baptist raised from the dead
questions.explanation: Herod thought Jesus was John the Baptist raised from the dead.

questions.text: 'Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.' The petitioners were
questions.explanation: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, made this request through their mother.

questions.text: 'Today salvation has come to this house, for this is also son of Abraham.' This was said of
questions.explanation: Jesus said this of Zacchaeus after he repented.

questions.text: In the parable of the ten maidens, the five were called foolish because they
options: were sleeping before the marriage feast
did not take additional oil with them
questions.explanation: The foolish virgins took no extra oil for their lamps.

questions.text: 'I find no crime in this man.' Who made this statement?
questions.explanation: Pilate said this after examining Jesus, finding no fault in Him.

questions.text: Concerning the events that will precede the end of the world, Jesus asked his followers to pray that it would not happen
questions.explanation: Jesus said to pray that their flight would not be in winter or on a Sabbath.

questions.text: Theophilus was
options: The one for whom the Acts of the Apostles was written
The centurion converted by Peter in Caesarea
questions.explanation: Luke wrote the Gospel and Acts to Theophilus.

questions.text: 'And the angel said to him, 'Dress yourself and put on your sandals'. The addressee was
questions.explanation: An angel said this to Peter when he was freed from prison.

questions.text: On the road to Gaza, Philip converted and baptized a

God's smiting of all the first born in Egypt

questions.text: The consecration of the people of Israel took place at the foot of Mount

options: Rejoicing for the water from the rock

The apostasy of Aaron and the people

options: summoned the elders and informed them about the land

have Solomon secretly anointed by Zadok
plead with Adonijah to abandon the attempt

the women of Israel were more beautiful
a King should not have too many children

The widow of Zarephath prepared food for Elijah
The widow and her son ate the food and waited for their death.
The woman was gathering sticks to prepare her last meal

questions.text: Who was that Egyptian king who not only made Eliakim king of Judah but changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim?

questions.text: Jeremiah wrote to the exiles in Babylon and encourages them to

questions.text: The order of the locations of Jesus' temptations according to Matthew is

options: waited two days before he obeyed
accounted for the tax he collected and responded
took some of the money he collected before following Him
questions.explanation: Levi (Matthew) left everything and followed Jesus.

questions.text: The miracle which touched on ingratitude is the

we should forgive our debtors from our hearts
debtors should be jailed until they pay all their debts.

questions.text: The ways in which various people hear the word of God are described in the parable of the

the kingdom of God has come upon you
the kingdom of Satan is already divided

questions.text: 'I assure you, unless you change and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of God.' This is a warning by Jesus against

questions.text: Jesus did not grant the request of the sons of Zebedee because
options: they were not qualified for the privilege they asked for
He did not want to encourage rivalry among the disciples
it was not His to grant the request
they could not drink with Jesus' cup.
questions.explanation: Jesus said it was not His to grant but belonged to the Father.

questions.text: The parable which teaches persistence in prayer is that of the
questions.explanation: The parable of the unjust judge teaches persistence in prayer.

questions.text: To give the widow's mite is to give

questions.text: Which of these women was absent during the crucifixion of Jesus Christ?

questions.text: To explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, Peter quoted Prophet

questions.text: 'Truly I perceive that God shows no partiality' was said by

questions.text: After the killing of James the son of Zebedee, Herod also arrested Peter because
options: Peter had promised to die with Jesus
the Jews were pleased with the murder of James
Herod wanted to show his zeal for the Law of Moses
Peter was the head of the Church

questions.text: The proconsul of Paphos during the visit of Paul and Barnabas was

questions.explanation: Lydia was converted at Philippi and hosted Paul and Silas.

questions.text: 'In a short time you think to make me a Christian' was said by

questions.text: 'Our sister, be the mother of thousands and ten thousands; and may your descendants possess...' Who was the sister?

questions.text: 'Cast out this slave woman with her son; for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.' Who was the slave woman?
questions.explanation: Sarah told Abraham to cast out Hagar and her son Ishmael.

options: it was the custom of his tribe to do so
God commanded him to do so
He wanted to distinguish Isaac from Ishmael
Isaac was the son of promise.

the death of the first born and beast
boils and sores on man and beast

questions.text: Whoever touches the 'mountain of God' shall be put to death by

Moses wanted to save them the trouble of searching for bread everyday
by then they had discovered a better way of preserving it.

questions.text: Who was regarded as the greatest prophet in the Old Testament for seeing God face to face?
questions.explanation: Moses is described as speaking to God face to face.

This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth
You shall select for yourself men of valour who will cross the Jordan with you.

questions.explanation: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu were invited to see God.

options: remind Israel of the crossing of River Jordan

questions.text: Samson, as a Nazarite, was required to avoid alcohol,

questions.explanation: Saul said this to Samuel after sparing Agag.

questions.text: Eli fell down and died because of the
options: capture of the Ark of Covenant

condemned Saul for offering sacrifice before his arrival

had been tricked by the wise men
could not see the new baby
searched in vain for the wise men

would realize little money from the sale of his goods

questions.text: Which religious groups asked Jesus about payment of taxes to Caesar?

questions.text: 'Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.' This leaven is their
questions.explanation: The leaven represents the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

questions.text: The three thousand converts on the day of Pentecost devoted themselves to
options: breaking of bread and the prayers
questions.explanation: The converts devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, breaking of bread, and prayers.

questions.text: Two of the seven deacons are
questions.explanation: Nicanor and Nicolas were two of the seven deacons.

questions.text: According to the apostle's speech before the Sanhedrin, the Holy Spirit is given by God to
questions.explanation: Peter said the Holy Spirit is given to those who obey God.

questions.text: In his speech concerning the replacement of Judas Iscariot, Peter quoted from
questions.explanation: Peter quoted from the Psalms concerning Judas' replacement.

questions.text: When Peter escaped from prison during the Passover, the guards were
questions.explanation: The guards were fast asleep when Peter escaped.

questions.text: One of the seven Hellenists who preached the gospel in Samaria, and from Azotus to the Syrian capital, Caesarea, was
questions.explanation: Philip the evangelist preached in Samaria and to the Ethiopian eunuch.

questions.text: Simon the magician was rebuked by Peter in Samaria because he
options: perverted the minds of the people
opposed the teaching of the apostles
wanted to purchase spiritual power with money
questions.explanation: Simon tried to buy the power of the Holy Spirit with money.

questions.text: The disciples were for the first time called Christians in
questions.explanation: The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

questions.text: 'Then the Lord God said, 'It is not good that the man should be alone;...'
questions.explanation: God said He would make a helper fit for Adam.

questions.text: The first generation of mankind was destroyed in the great flood of water because of
questions.explanation: The earth was corrupt and filled with violence, so God destroyed it.

questions.text: Which of the following is the sign of the covenant between God and Abraham?
options: The sprinkling of blood on door posts
Circumcision in the flesh of the foreskins

questions.text: God appeared to Jacob in a dream and Jacob made a vow to
questions.explanation: Jacob vowed to give a tenth of all he had to God.

questions.text: Joseph saw his sale by his brothers as God's plan to enable him
questions.explanation: Joseph saw God's plan as preserving life during the famine.

questions.text: The two Hebrew midwives instructed by Pharaoh to kill the Hebrew male babies at birth were
questions.explanation: The midwives were Shiphrah and Puah.

questions.text: The Egyptian magicians were able to reproduce the first three miracles done by Moses and Aaron, but the fourth which they were unable to perform was the plague of
questions.explanation: The magicians could not reproduce the plague of gnats.

questions.text: The possibility of crossing the Red Sea was seen by Israel as
options: God's active presence in their midst
the miraculous power of Moses' rod
questions.explanation: Israel saw the crossing as God's active presence among them.

questions.text: In Exodus 17 and Numbers 20, similar incidents of lack of water for the congregation are recorded. A significant difference however, is that in Exodus 17, Moses is commanded to
